title: Imran Khan Calls on Bollywood to Embrace Dissent, Joins Student Protests Across India
excerpt: The actor, who returned to public life after an 11-year hiatus, has become one of Bollywood's most prominent voices supporting the ongoing NEET student movement.
body:
• Bollywood actor Imran Khan has participated in NEET student protests in Mumbai and voiced support for demonstrations in Jharkhand
  • Khan criticized fellow actors for remaining apolitical, saying art that avoids personal conviction "has no value"
  • His activism marks a sharp turn for an actor who stepped away from films in 2015 and is now making a comeback with Netflix's Adhure Hum Adhure Tum
  • The NEET protests over alleged exam irregularities have drawn participation from students and public figures across India since July 2026

Bollywood actor Imran Khan has emerged as one of the film industry's most vocal supporters of the student protest movement that has swept across India in recent weeks. Khan, who is preparing a comeback after an 11-year absence from films, has participated in protest marches in Mumbai and publicly backed student demonstrations in Jharkhand, drawing both praise and scrutiny for his willingness to wade into political territory.

On the Streets and Online

Khan joined a NEET student protest in Mumbai in late July, marching alongside demonstrators who allege widespread irregularities in the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test examination system. In a video shared by aspiring actress Riya Jana on Instagram, Khan addressed the role of artists in public discourse.

"True art is going to have an individual artist's point of view embedded within it. If you can't stand by your opinions and if you do not pour your own heart into your art, your art has no value."

— Imran Khan, actor

His comments were directed at fellow Bollywood figures who have chosen to remain silent on political and social issues. In the Indian film industry, where speaking out can carry professional consequences, Khan's stance has drawn attention for its directness, according to Bollywood Hungama.

On social media, Khan has been equally blunt. After police action against student demonstrators, he wrote: "Something broke in me today watching police gas and batter student protesters. How could I make sense of this? These students who worked hard only to be failed by the system." On August 5, he backed protests in Jharkhand with a characteristically sardonic post: "Students protesting in Jharkhand. Let's all ignore them, what could possibly go wrong," according to Filmfare.

A Comeback Shaped by Conviction

Khan's activism is arriving alongside his professional return. The nephew of actor Aamir Khan, he made his debut as a lead in the 2008 hit Jaane Tu... Ya Jaane Na and built a following with films including Delhi Belly and I Hate Luv Storys. After his 2015 film Katti Batti, he stepped away from acting entirely.

In interviews, Khan has described that period as a time of emotional reckoning. "I realised I was scared and emotionally closed off," he told Filmfare. "Admitting that and committing to emotional and psychological growth became a turning point for me around mid-2016."

He confirmed his return to acting earlier this month with the Netflix film Adhure Hum Adhure Tum. The timing of his comeback — alongside rather than separate from his protest activity — suggests an actor who views public engagement as inseparable from creative work.

The Wider Movement

The NEET protests have drawn participation from other Bollywood figures as well. Actor Rajkummar Rao called for dialogue and peaceful resolution, while singer Arijit Singh was sharply critical of police action against students. Actor Vedang Raina expressed pride at being "part of a generation that cares" and isn't afraid to show up, according to Filmfare.

For the Indian diaspora, the NEET controversy touches on long-standing concerns about the fairness and transparency of India's competitive examination system — a system that has shaped the educational trajectories of millions of Indian-origin professionals worldwide.
